problem: VLN tasks use text-only instructions, which are abstract and ambiguous (e.g. an unfamiliar object like 'wicker chair'). Prior work provides no way for an agent to use image prompts as part of the instruction, and no benchmark or model exists for this.
motivation: In real-world navigation humans routinely combine photos with short descriptions (maps, phone cameras), and images are easy to obtain. Visual prompts can disambiguate targets and reduce the reliance on perfect language instructions, so agents should handle varying numbers and relevance of images.
key_idea: Define VLN with Multi-modal Prompts (VLN-MP): interleave landmark images into instructions, build them with a training-free LLM/detector pipeline, and fuse them with text through a Multi-modal Prompts Fusion (MPF) module plugged into HAMT/DUET.
insight: Performance on RxR-MP rises with the number and relevance of images (Terminal < Related < Aligned pipeline < Aligned Marky-mT5), yet the agent still works with text only, so it remains backward compatible. In goal-oriented CVDN-MP, a target image helps more than a BLIP2 caption in unseen houses. Ablations show both position encodings (VPE + MPE) contribute, and ControlNet augmentation at gamma=0.2 helps val-unseen but hurts val-seen.
method: Extraction: GPT-4 with crafted prompts extracts landmark phrases from instructions.
Detection: GroundingDINO (short or object-centric instructions) or GLIP (long instructions) zero-shot scans all views along the GT path and yields candidates (score, image, box).

Alignment: Related picks the highest detection score. Aligned maximizes S_all = S_s (Kendall sequence score) + 0.5*S_d + 0.1*S_b (box size) with adaptive bidirectional beam search. Terminal uses only the last landmark image.
Augmentation: ControlNet conditioned on M-LSD line segments generates 5 novel images per landmark image, which replace the originals with probability 0.2 during training.

MPF module: an image encoder plus type and position embeddings gives image tokens, which are merged with text tokens, receive a second (multimodal) position embedding, and pass through a multi-layer Transformer. Plugs into HAMT and DUET.
Datasets: R2R-MP, RxR-MP (plus Marky-mT5 alternative Aligned), REVERIE-MP (from box annotations), CVDN-MP (dialogue removed, with BLIP2 captions as an alternative).

Pre-explore use: the agent first follows the text to a pseudo path, extracts landmark images from the visited nodes and neighbors with the pipeline, then re-navigates with the multi-modal instruction.

setting.backbone: HAMT and DUET with MPF module (fine-tuned); pipeline uses GPT-4, GLIP-L, GroundingDINO-T, ControlNet
setting.training_data: R2R-MP, RxR-MP, REVERIE-MP and CVDN-MP training splits (landmark images from the pipeline plus 5 ControlNet-augmented images per prompt); fine-tuned 200K iterations, lr 1e-5, batch 8, one A6000
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) plus instruction text interleaved with landmark images
setting.privileged: Landmark images for evaluation are generated from the GT path (dataset construction); pre-explore setting uses a pseudo path from a previous run

results: On RxR-MP, HAMT+MPF improves with more and better-aligned images, reaching 60.0 SR / 56.3 SPL on val-unseen with Marky-mT5 Aligned images versus 56.5 / 56.0 for HAMT text-only. On CVDN-MP, image+text raises GP to 3.11 (HAMT) and 4.13 (DUET) on val-unseen. Pre-explore with VLN-MP gives +6.9 SR (seen) and +2.5 SR (unseen) over the original HAMT on RxR.
limitations: Test images are generated from GT paths, so the settings are somewhat idealized; the pre-explore setting needs an extra trial
Only HAMT and DUET are tested. R2R-MP and REVERIE-MP results are not shown, so evidence is mostly RxR and CVDN
SPL on val-unseen is not consistently better than the text-only baseline
